occupations.cat: Building and related trades workers, excluding electricians

n.story:
In a world of increasing automation, your role remains a bastion of human craftsmanship, but with a high-tech edge. While robots may handle long, straight stretches of warehouse walling, your expertise is redirected toward the complex, irregular, and bespoke elements of construction that require human touch and spatial problem-solving. You will spend significantly less time on the 'grunt work'—sorting through waste, mixing mortar by hand, or interpreting confusing 2D blueprints—as AI-driven tools take over these repetitive tasks.

Your workflow will be amplified by augmented reality (AR) headsets that project 3D blueprints directly onto your workspace, showing you exactly where every brick and profile needs to go with millimeter precision. You will become a specialist who manages the 'edge cases' of the site, using AI to verify the quality of supplies and ensure that safety protocols are met in real-time. You are no longer just laying bricks; you are a precision technician ensuring the structural and aesthetic integrity of complex builds.

Real-time safety hazard identification
Material defect detection via computer vision
Optimized site navigation and supply logistics
n.adv: Embrace digital layout tools and AR interfaces. As simple bricklaying becomes more automated, your ability to work with complex digital plans will distinguish you as a master tradesperson.
